source_text:
Sententiae ad monachos
Πρὸς τοὺς ἐν κοινοβίοις ἢ συνοδίαις μοναχούς.
1 Κληρονόμοι θεοῦ ἀκούσατε λόγων θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ
δέξασθε ῥήσεις Χριστοῦ, ἵνα δῶτε αὐτὰς καρδίαις τέκνων ὑμῶν, λόγους δὲ σοφῶν
διδάξητε αὐτούς.
2 Πατὴρ ἀγαθὸς παιδεύει υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, πατὴρ δὲ πονηρὸς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς.
3 Πίστις ἀρχὴ ἀγάπης, τέλος δὲ ἀγάπης γνῶσις θεοῦ.
4 Φόβος κυρίου διατηρήσει ψυχήν, ἐγκράτεια δὲ ἀγαθὴ ἐνισχύσει αὐτήν.
5 Ὑπομονὴ ἀνδρὸς τίκτει ἐλπίδα, ἐλπὶς δὲ ἀγαθὴ δοξάσει αὐτόν.
6 Ὁ δουλαγωγῶν σάρκας αὐτοῦ ἀπαθὴς ἔσται, ὁ δὲ ἐκτρέφων αὐτὰς
ὀδυνηθήσεται ἐπ' αὐταῖς.
7 Πνεῦμα πορνείας ἐν σώμασιν ἀκρατῶν, πνεῦμα δὲ σωφροσύνης ἐν ψυχαῖς
ἐγκρατῶν.
8 Ἀναχώρησις ἐν ἀγάπῃ καθαίρει καρδίαν, ἀναχώρησις δὲ μετὰ μίσους
ἐκταράσσει αὐτήν.
9 Κρείσσων χιλιοστὸς ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἢ μόνος μετὰ μίσους ἐν ἀδύτοις σπηλαίοις.
10 Ὁ ἐναποδεσμεύων μνησικακίαν ἐν ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ ὅμοιός ἐστι τῷ κρύπτοντι
πῦρ ἐν ἀχύροις.
11 Μὴ δῷς βρώματα πολλὰ τῷ σώματί σου, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδῃς καθ' ὕπνους
φαντασίας κακάς. ὃν τρόπον γὰρ φλὸξ καταναλίσκει δρυμόν, οὕτω φαντασίας
αἰσχρὰς σβέννυσι πεῖνα.
12 Ἀνὴρ θυμώδης πτοηθήσεται, ὁ δὲ πραῢς ἄφοβος ἔσται.
3 Ἄνεμος σφοδρὸς ἀποδιώκει νέφη, μνησικακία δὲ τὸν νοῦν ἀπὸ γνώσεως.
14 Ὁ προσευχόμενος ὑπὲρ ἐχθρῶν ἀμνησίκακος ἔσται, φειδόμενος δὲ
γλώσσης οὐ λυπήσει τὸν πλησίον αὐτοῦ.
15 Ἐὰν παροξύνῃ σε ὁ ἀδελφός σου, εἰσάγαγε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου, καὶ
πρὸς αὐτὸν μὴ ὀκνήσῃς εἰσελθεῖν, ἀλλὰ φάγε τὸν ψωμόν σου μετ' αὐτοῦ. τοῦτο γὰρ
ποιῶν ῥύσῃ σὴν ψυχὴν καὶ οὐκ ἔσται σοι πρόσκομμα ἐν καιρῷ προσευχῆς.
16 Ὥσπερ ἡ ἀγάπη χαίρει πενίᾳ, οὕτω τὸ μῖσος τέρπεται πλούτῳ.
17 Οὐκ ἐπιτεύξεται πλούσιος γνώσεως καὶ κάμηλος οὐκ εἰσελεύσεται εἰς
ὀπὴν ῥαφίδος, ἀλλ' οὐδὲν τούτων ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ κυρίῳ
18 Ὁ φιλῶν ἀργύριον οὐκ ὄψεται γνῶσιν, καὶ ὁ συνάγων αὐτὸ
σκοτισθήσεται.
19 Ἐν σκηναῖς ταπεινῶν αὐλισθήσεται κύριος, ἐν οἴκοις δὲ ὑπερηφάνων
πληθυνθήσονται ἀραί.
20 Ἀτιμάζει θεὸν ὁ παραβαίνων νόμον αὐτοῦ, ὁ δὲ φυλάσσων αὐτὸν δοξάζει
τὸν ποιήσαντα αὐτόν.
21 Ἐὰν ζηλώσῃς Χριστόν, γενήσῃ μακαριστός, τὸν δὲ θάνατον αὐτοῦ
ἀποθανεῖται ἡ ψυχή σου, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐπισπάσηται ἀπὸ σαρκὸς αὐτῆς κακίαν, ἀλλ'
ἔσται ἡ ἔξοδός σου ὡς ἔξοδος ἀστέρος, καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασίς σου ὥσπερ ὁ ἥλιος ἐκλάμψει.
22 Οὐαὶ ἀνόμῳ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θανάτου, καὶ ἄδικος ὀλεῖται ἐν καιρῷ πονηρῷ. ὃν
τρόπον γὰρ ἀφίπταται κόραξ ἐκ τῆς αὐτοῦ νοσσιᾶς, οὕτως ἀκάθαρτος ψυχὴ ἐκ τοῦ
ἰδίου σώματος.
23 Ψυχὰς δικαίων ὁδηγοῦσιν ἄγγελοι, ψυχὰς δὲ πονηρῶν παραλήψονται
δαίμονες.
1
24 Οὗ ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ κακία, ἐκεῖ καὶ ἀγνωσία, καρδίαι δὲ ὁσίων πληρωθήσονται
γνώσεως.
25 Ἀνελεήμων μοναχὸς ἐνδεὴς ἔσται, διατρέφων δὲ πτωχοὺς κληρονομήσει
θησαυρούς.
26 Κρείσσων πενία μετὰ γνώσεως ἢ πλοῦτος μετὰ ἀγνωσίας.
27 Κόσμος κεφαλῆς στέφανος, κόσμος δὲ καρδίας γνῶσις θεοῦ.
28 Κτῆσαι γνῶσιν καὶ μὴ ἀργύριον καὶ σοφίαν ὑπὲρ πλοῦτον πολύν.
29 ∆ίκαιοι κληρονομήσουσι κύριον, ὅσιοι δὲ τραφήσονται ὑπ' αὐτοῦ.
30 Ὁ ἐλεῶν πένητας διαφθείρει θυμόν, καὶ ὁ διατρέφων αὐτοὺς πλησθήσεται
ἀγαθῶν.
31 Ἐν καρδίᾳ πραείᾳ ἀναπαύσεται σοφία, θρόνος δὲ ἀπαθείας ψυχὴ πρακτική.
32 Τέκτονες πονηρῶν λήψονται μισθὸν κακόν, τέκτοσι δὲ ἀγαθῶν δοθήσεται
μισθὸς ἀγαθός.
33 Ὁ τιθεὶς παγίδα συλληφθήσεται ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ ὁ κρύπτων αὐτὴν ἁλώσεται
ὑπ' αὐτῆς.
34 Κρείσσων κοσμικὸς πραῢς μοναχοῦ θυμώδους καὶ ὀργίλου.
35 Γνῶσιν διασκορπίζει θυμός, μακροθυμία δὲ συνάγει αὐτήν.
36 Ὥσπερ νότος ἰσχυρὸς ἐν πελάγει οὕτως θυμὸς ἐν καρδίᾳ ἀνδρός.
37 Ὁ προσευχόμενος συνεχῶς ἐκφεύγει πειρασμούς, ἀμελοῦντος δὲ καρδίαν
ἐκταράσσουσι λογισμοί.
38 Μὴ εὐφραινέτω σε οἶνος καὶ μὴ τερπέτω σε κρέας, ἵνα μὴ διαθρέψῃς
σάρκας σώματός σου, καὶ λογισμοὶ αἰσχροὶ οὐκ ἐκλείψουσιν ἀπό σου.
thought_title: Opening exhortation and first sayings on virtue, passion, and knowledge
orientation: Evagrius opens his collection of sayings by addressing monks who live in communities, calling them heirs of God and urging them to receive and pass on divine words.
pass_a_gloss: To the monks in cenobia or communities. [You] heirs of God, hear words of God, and [you] co-heirs of Christ, receive sayings of Christ, so that you may give them to [the] hearts of your children, and [that] you may teach them words of wise men. [A] good father disciplines his sons, but [a] wicked father will destroy them. Faith [is the] beginning of love, and [the] end of love [is] knowledge of God. [The] fear of [the] Lord will preserve [the] soul, and good self-control will strengthen it. [The] endurance of [a] man gives birth to hope, and good hope will glorify him. [The one] enslaving his flesh will be free from passions, but [the one] nourishing it will be pained over it. [The] spirit of fornication [is] in [the] bodies of [the] self-indulgent, but [the] spirit of self-control [is] in [the] souls of [the] self-controlled. Withdrawal in love cleanses [the] heart, but withdrawal with hatred disturbs it. Better [is] [the] thousandth in love than alone with hatred in inner caves. [The one] binding resentment in his soul is like [the one] hiding fire in chaff. Do not give many foods to your body, and you will not see evil fantasies in sleep. For as [a] flame consumes [a] thicket, so hunger extinguishes shameful fantasies. [A] wrathful man will be terrified, but [the] gentle [man] will be fearless. [A] strong wind drives away clouds, and resentment [drives away] the mind from knowledge. [The one] praying for enemies will be without resentment, and [the one] sparing [his] tongue will not grieve his neighbor. If your brother provokes you, bring him into your house, and do not hesitate to go in to him, but eat your morsel with him. For [the one] doing this will deliver his soul, and there will not be for you [a] stumbling block in [the] time of prayer. As love rejoices in poverty, so hatred delights in wealth. [A] rich [man] will not attain knowledge, and [a] camel will not enter into [the] eye of [a] needle, but none of these will be impossible with [the] Lord. [The one] loving silver will not see knowledge, and [the one] gathering it will be darkened. In [the] tents of [the] humble [the] Lord will lodge, but in [the] houses of [the] proud curses will be multiplied. [The one] transgressing his law dishonors God, but [the one] keeping it glorifies [the one] who made it. If you are zealous for Christ, you will be blessed, and your soul will die his death, and it will not draw wickedness from its flesh, but your departure will be as [the] departure of [a] star, and your resurrection will shine as [the] sun. Woe to [the] lawless [man] in [the] day of death, and [the] unjust [man] will perish in [an] evil time. For as [a] raven flies away from its nest, so [an] unclean soul [flies away] from its own body. [The] souls of [the] righteous angels guide, but [the] souls of [the] wicked demons will take. Where wickedness enters, there also [is] ignorance, but [the] hearts of [the] holy will be filled with knowledge. [An] unmerciful monk will be needy, but [the one] feeding [the] poor will inherit treasures. Better [is] poverty with knowledge than wealth with ignorance. [The] ornament of [the] head [is a] crown, but [the] ornament of [the] heart [is] knowledge of God. Acquire knowledge and not silver, and wisdom above much wealth. [The] righteous will inherit [the] Lord, and [the] holy will be nourished by him. [The one] showing mercy to [the] poor destroys anger, and [the one] feeding them will be filled with good things. In [a] gentle heart wisdom will rest, and [the] throne of freedom from passions [is] [the] active soul. [The] builders of evil things will receive [an] evil wage, but to [the] builders of good things [a] good wage will be given. [The one] setting [a] trap will be caught in it, and [the one] hiding it will be captured by it. Better [is a] gentle worldly [man] than [a] wrathful and irascible monk. Anger scatters knowledge, but patience gathers it. As [a] strong south wind [is] in [the] sea, so [is] anger in [the] heart of [a] man. [The one] praying continually escapes temptations, but [the] heart of [the one] neglecting [prayer] thoughts disturb. Let not wine gladden you and let not meat delight you, so that you may not nourish [the] flesh of your body, and shameful thoughts will not depart from you.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'freedom from passions' for ἀπάθεια; the adjective form is rendered to match.
Glossary requires 'knowledge' for γνῶσις, the spiritual knowledge of God.
Glossary requires 'resentment' for μνησικακία, holding onto grudges.
Glossary requires 'active life' for πρακτική; here it modifies ψυχή, so 'active soul' preserves the term.
Glossary requires 'gentleness' for πραΰτης; the adjective form is rendered to match.

bible_refs.note: κάμηλος οὐκ εἰσελεύσεται εἰς ὀπὴν ῥαφίδος
ἐν σκηναῖς ταπεινῶν αὐλισθήσεται κύριος, ἐν οἴκοις δὲ ὑπερηφάνων

pass_b_english: Heirs of God, listen to the words of God. Co-heirs of Christ, receive the sayings of Christ, so that you may give them to the hearts of your children and teach them the words of the wise.
A good father instructs his sons, but a wicked father will destroy them.
Faith is the beginning of love, and the end of love is knowledge of God.
The fear of the Lord will preserve the soul, and good self-control will strengthen it.
A man's endurance gives birth to hope, and good hope will glorify him.
The one who enslaves his flesh will be free from passions, but the one who indulges it will suffer pain because of it.
A spirit of fornication dwells in the bodies of the self-indulgent, but a spirit of self-control dwells in the souls of the self-controlled.
Withdrawal in love purifies the heart, but withdrawal with hatred throws it into confusion.
Better to be one in a thousand with love than alone with hatred in hidden caves.
The one who stores up resentment in his soul is like someone hiding fire in straw.
Do not give your body too much food, and you will not see evil fantasies in your sleep. For just as a flame consumes a forest, so hunger extinguishes shameful fantasies.
A wrathful man will be terrified, but the gentle man will be without fear.
A strong wind drives away clouds, and resentment drives the mind away from knowledge.
The one who prays for his enemies will be without resentment, and the one who guards his tongue will not grieve his neighbor.

If your brother provokes you, bring him into your house, and do not hesitate to go to him, but eat your morsel with him. For by doing this you will rescue your soul, and there will be no stumbling block for you in the time of prayer.
Just as love rejoices in poverty, so hatred delights in wealth.
A rich man will not attain knowledge, and a camel will not enter the eye of a needle, but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24, 26; Mark 10:25, 27).
The one who loves silver will not see knowledge, and the one who hoards it will be darkened.
The Lord will dwell in the tents of the humble, but curses will multiply in the houses of the proud (Proverbs 3:33).
The one who transgresses God's law dishonors God, but the one who keeps it glorifies the one who made it.

If you are zealous for Christ, you will be blessed, and your soul will share his death, and it will not draw evil from its flesh, but your departure will be like the departure of a star, and your resurrection will shine like the sun.
Woe to the lawless man on the day of death, and the unjust man will perish in an evil time. For just as a raven flies away from its nest, so an unclean soul departs from its own body.
Angels guide the souls of the righteous, but demons will seize the souls of the wicked.
Wherever evil enters, there also is ignorance, but the hearts of the holy will be filled with knowledge.
A merciless monk will be in need, but the one who feeds the poor will inherit treasures.
Better is poverty with knowledge than wealth with ignorance.
A crown is the ornament of the head, but knowledge of God is the ornament of the heart.
Acquire knowledge and not silver, and wisdom rather than great wealth.
The righteous will inherit the Lord, and the holy will be nourished by him.
The one who has mercy on the poor destroys anger, and the one who feeds them will be filled with good things.
Wisdom will rest in a gentle heart, and an active soul is the throne of freedom from passions.
Craftsmen of evil will receive an evil wage, but craftsmen of good will be given a good wage.
The one who sets a trap will be caught in it, and the one who hides it will be captured by it.
Better is a gentle worldly man than a wrathful and irascible monk.
Anger scatters knowledge, but patience gathers it.
As a strong south wind on the open sea, so is anger in a man's heart.
The one who prays continually escapes temptations, but thoughts trouble the heart of the negligent one.
Do not let wine gladden you, and do not let meat delight you, so that you do not nourish the flesh of your body, and shameful thoughts will not cease from you.

problems.quote: so that you do not nourish the flesh of your body, and shameful thoughts will not depart from you
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ διαθρέψῃς σάρκας σώματός σου, καὶ λογισμοὶ αἰσχροὶ οὐκ ἐκλείψουσιν ἀπό σου
problems.why: Final clause should be positive command: 'so that shameful thoughts cease,' not negative 'will not depart'.
problems.fix: so that you do not nourish the flesh of your body, and shameful thoughts will cease from you.

problems.source_quote: ἀλλ' οὐδὲν τούτων ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ κυρίῳ
problems.why: The camel/needle saying is Mark 10:25/Matthew 19:24, but 'nothing will be impossible with the Lord' is Luke 1:37 (also Matthew 19:26). The parenthetical citation misattributes the second clause.

problems.source_quote: Ἐν σκηναῖς ταπεινῶν αὐλισθήσεται κύριος, ἐν οἴκοις δὲ ὑπερηφάνων πληθυνθήσονται ἀραί

edits.old: so that you do not nourish the flesh of your body, and shameful thoughts will not depart from you.
edits.new: so that you do not nourish the flesh of your body, and shameful thoughts will cease from you.

fixed: Final clause corrected to positive command: 'shameful thoughts will cease from you.'
Scripture citation corrected to include Luke 1:37 for 'nothing will be impossible with the Lord.'

problems.source_quote: ἀλλ' οὐδὲν τούτων ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ κυρίῳ
problems.why: Luke 1:37 is wrong; the camel/needle saying is Matthew 19:24/Mark 10:25/Luke 18:25, and 'nothing impossible with the Lord' matches Matthew 19:26/Mark 10:27/Luke 18:27.

edits.old: but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24; Luke 1:37).
edits.new: but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:26; Mark 10:27).

fixed: Replaced the incorrect scripture citation Luke 1:37 with Matthew 19:26 and Mark 10:27, which match the saying about nothing being impossible with the Lord.

problems.why: ἐν πελάγει means 'on the open sea', not 'stirs the sea'—the wind blows on the sea.
problems.fix: As a strong south wind on the open sea, so anger in a man's heart.

problems.quote: thoughts trouble the heart of the negligent
problems.why: ἀμελοῦντος is genitive absolute 'of the negligent one', but 'heart of the negligent' makes 'negligent' adjectival—slight shift.
problems.fix: but thoughts trouble the heart of the negligent one.

problems.why: οὐκ ἐκλείψουσιν means 'will not cease/fail', but English says 'will cease'—negation flipped!
problems.fix: and shameful thoughts will not cease from you.
problems.ruling: οὐκ ἐκλείψουσιν means 'will NOT cease'; English 'will cease' flips the negation

problems.source_quote: οὐκ εἰσελεύσεται εἰς ὀπὴν ῥαφίδος, ἀλλ' οὐδὲν τούτων ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ κυρίῳ
problems.why: The camel/needle saying is Matthew 19:24/Mark 10:25; 19:26/10:27 is 'with God all things are possible'.
problems.ruling: Camel/needle is Matt 19:24/Mark 10:25; 19:26/10:27 is 'with God all things possible'—wrong reference

edits.old: As a strong south wind stirs the sea, so anger stirs a man's heart.
edits.new: As a strong south wind on the open sea, so is anger in a man's heart.

edits.old: but thoughts trouble the heart of the negligent.
edits.new: but thoughts trouble the heart of the negligent one.

edits.old: and shameful thoughts will cease from you.
edits.new: and shameful thoughts will not cease from you.

edits.old: but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:26; Mark 10:27).
edits.new: but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24; Mark 10:25).

fixed: The south wind problem was real: the source says the wind is on the open sea, not that it stirs the sea.
The negligent problem was real: the source uses a genitive absolute referring to a person, so 'negligent one' is more accurate.
The cease problem was real: the source has a negated verb, so the English must say 'will not cease'.
The scripture problem was real: the camel/needle saying is Matthew 19:24 and Mark 10:25, not the verses about all things being possible.

problems.why: Reader may think 'free from passions' and 'freedom from passions' differ.
Noun and adjective forms are fine, but 'self-control' vs 'self-controlled' as group label unclear.
Bare 'knowledge' vs 'knowledge of God' vs 'true knowledge' vs 'false knowledge'—reader may not connect these as related technical terms.
problems.fix: Consistently qualify or explain that 'knowledge' alone means 'knowledge of God'.

problems.quote: A rich man will not attain knowledge, and a camel will not enter the eye of a needle, but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24; Mark 10:25)
problems.why: The 'nothing will be impossible with the Lord' clause is from Matthew 19:26/Mark 10:27, not 19:24/10:25; citation conflates two verses.

problems.quote: A rich man will not attain knowledge, and a camel will not enter the eye of a needle, but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24; Mark 10:25)
problems.why: Matthew 19:24 is correct; Mark 10:25 is correct; but 'nothing impossible with the Lord' is from Matthew 19:26 / Mark 10:27, not cited.
problems.fix: Add Matthew 19:26 or Mark 10:27 for the final clause.

edits.old: A rich man will not attain knowledge, and a camel will not enter the eye of a needle, but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24; Mark 10:25).
edits.new: A rich man will not attain knowledge, and a camel will not enter the eye of a needle, but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24, 26; Mark 10:25, 27).

fixed: The glossary issue about 'freedom from passions' is not a problem in the English text; the English consistently uses 'free from passions' as an adjective phrase and 'freedom from passions' as a noun phrase, which is natural.
The glossary issue about 'self-control' is not a problem in the English text; 'self-control' and 'self-controlled' are used naturally as noun and adjective.
The glossary issue about 'knowledge of God' is not a problem in the English text; the English uses 'knowledge' and 'knowledge of God' naturally according to the source wording.
The scripture citation was corrected to include the verses for the final clause.

polish.changed: Clarified the ambiguous phrase about the soul's death to 'your soul will share his death,' and kept all other wording faithful to the source while preserving the glossary terms exactly.

notes.why: Six different renderings for Greek askesis/energeia/aretai related terms obscure they are one technical progression.
notes.fix: Use consistent technical terms with glosses.

notes.why: Reader cannot distinguish generic knowledge from technical gnosis or its hierarchical levels.
Same Greek root (orge/lype) rendered as resentment, anger, wrath, irascible—reader may miss connection.
Acedia (listlessness) is a specific demon; 'sluggish' and 'sleepy' blur this technical term.

notes.quote: your soul will die his death
notes.why: Probably means 'die to sin with Christ' or 'share his death,' not soul actually dying.
notes.fix: Render as 'your soul will die with him' or 'be crucified with him'.

notes.why: Citation covers verses 24 and 26 but quotes only 'camel through eye of needle' and 'nothing impossible with God'—verse 25 omitted in citation, verse 26 cited without 'with God this is possible'.
notes.fix: Adjust citation to Matthew 19:24, 26 or quote fully.

dismissed.why: Glossary mandates 'active life' for πρακτική, not 'active soul'.
dismissed.note: psyche praktike = the soul engaged in the practical (ascetic) life; "active soul" is acceptable and glossary pedantry does not change meaning.
